call.x: Apply for funding to purchase mid-range equipment for research across BBSRC’s scientific remit through ALERT 2026. You must be based at a UK research organisation eligible for BBSRC funding. Research technical professionals are eligible as project leads or project co-leads for this funding opportunity.
n: Run by Biotechnology and Biological Sciences Research Council (BBSRC). The organiser sets the rules; Eligible Calls reads this call from UKRI Funding Finder (ukri.org).

UKRI-mid-range-equipment-for-biosciences.heading: How we will assess your application

blocks.text: Assessment process
We will assess your application using the following process. We reserve the right to modify the assessment process as needed.
Expert panel

Assessment will be conducted by a multidisciplinary panel of experts covering scientific, managerial, technical and user aspects of equipment provision and management. Additional external reviews will not be sought.

Panel members will assess the application independently against the published criteria for this funding opportunity, making an evidence-based judgement and scoring the application based on their expertise.

The panel will discuss and agree a consensus score using a scoring table. The score agreed by the panel and, based on how well the assessment criteria have been met, will be used to group applications into tiers.
Decisions based on tiers
We will use a tiered approach to make decisions, using assessment tools such as randomisation and strategic allocation so that the aims of the funding opportunity are met.
If a tiered approach is used, applications are assigned to one of three tiers:
tier one, the highest quality, prioritised for funding
tier two, highly competitive, selected by assessment tools and dependent on remaining budget
tier three, not competitive enough to be considered for funding
If tiers are not practical, a ranked list is formed based on the order of overall score from highest to lowest. Funding will be allocated down the list until the budget runs out.
For more information on how we prioritise applications for funding please visit How we make decisions .
Budget considerations

The indicative budget for this funding opportunity forms part of a wider funding allocation that supports world class bioscience resources, equipment and facilities. In making funding decisions, we may consider the balance, quality and strategic alignment of the combined portfolio of applications across funding opportunities. As such, we reserve the right to adjust allocations accordingly and the final budget under this funding opportunity may differ from the indicative budget stated.
Timescale
We aim to complete the assessment process within four months of receiving your application.
Feedback
We will give feedback with the outcome of your application.
Principles of assessment
We support the San Francisco declaration on research assessment and recognise the relationship between research assessment and research integrity.
Find out about the UKRI principles of assessment and decision making .
Using generative artificial intelligence (AI) in expert review

Generative AI may only be used for the purpose of language refinement during application assessment. When using generative AI to refine the language of a review, expert reviewers and panellists must ensure that:
no part of the application being assessed is entered into a generative AI tool
no personal information from the application is disclosed
generative AI is not tasked with understanding, summarising or evaluating the application’s content
Expert reviewers and panellists must also:
comply with relevant intellectual property and data protection legislation
not take into account or speculate within their assessment whether generative AI has been used to develop the application
For more detail see our policy on the use of generative AI .
Assessment areas
The assessment areas we will use are:
purpose
vision
approach
sustainability
applicant and team capability to deliver
resources and costs
ethics and responsible research and innovation (RRI): informed by animal involvement and ‘3Rs’, genetically modified organisms and biological risk, and human participation in health-related research

While the following areas will not affect the overall quality score, assessors will be asked to provide their view on the following areas. Any award may be dependent on addressing concerns raised in these sections:
trusted research and innovation
your organisation’s support
project partners
data management and sharing
Find details of assessment questions and criteria under the ‘Application questions’ heading in the ‘How to apply’ section.

consortium.quote: Unless otherwise provided for in the specific call/topic conditions, only legal entities forming a consortium are eligible to participate in actions provided that the consortium includes, as beneficiaries, three legal entities independent from each other and each established in a different country as follows: – at least one independent legal entity established in a Member State; and – at least two other independent legal entities, each established in different Member States or Associated Countries.
